sections.html:
Up in Oklahoma's northeast corner, with Kansas on its northern edge, Craig County has Vinita for a seat and 14,104 residents as of 2020. Bluejacket, Big Cabin, Ketchum, Vinita and Welch are the five towns. One Treasurer bills every house in the county, and only the city and school levies differ from town to town.

A Craig County parcel might be a town lot, a few acres of pasture or a hay field, and each kind has its own tax paperwork. Older homes and rural land are common, and plenty of owners live elsewhere after inheriting from family. Interstate 44 and U.S. Highways 59, 60 and 69 cross the county. Vinita is about sixty miles from Tulsa and sixty from Joplin, Missouri.

Two offices split the work: the Assessor sets the value, and the Treasurer collects the tax. What the Assessor certifies on real estate, personal property and public utilities goes to the Treasurer, who passes it along to the county, towns and school districts under budgets set by the Excise Board. The rate on your bill is a blend of several levies, and the Treasurer has no say in it.

Craig County Treasurer contact details
Contact pointCraig County Treasurer
Office210 W. Delaware, Suite 104, Vinita, OK 74301; 918-256-2286
HoursMonday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM
Drop boxNear the west doors of the courthouse
Online lookupTax roll inquiry on oktaxrolls.com

Holiday closures happen through the year, so phone ahead before a counter visit near one.

State law (68 O.S. 2913) sets two deadlines. One half is due ahead of January 1 and the other ahead of April 1. If less than half is in by December 31, the full year's levy is delinquent as of January 1. Questions about your own account go to the Treasurer.

  • If no statement reaches you, the deadline stays where it is.
  • An older balance may be noted on the statement, which means the printed figure can understate what you owe.
  • When you owe back taxes, ask for a written total that holds through the day you expect to close.

Disputes start at the Assessor's desk. A written protest is due within 30 calendar days after the valuation notice went out in the mail, under Form 974 and 68 O.S. 2876.

  1. Submit Form 974 with your own opinion of market value.
  2. Support it with proof such as a recent sale, comps or an appraisal.
  3. Take part in the informal hearing, which can be done by phone on request.
  4. The Assessor owes you a written decision inside seven calendar days of the hearing.
  5. Still unhappy? Form 976 goes to the county board of equalization within 15 calendar days of the decision's mailing.

If your value did not move from last year, you may protest until the first Monday in April. The board wraps up by May 31 or its adjournment date. Let the 30 days lapse and the proposed value holds for that tax year. Go by the date on your own notice.

sections.h2: Unpaid city charges on the tax account
sections.html:
If a town's weed, cleanup, paving or nuisance abatement charge goes unpaid, the town certifies it to the County Treasurer, and it becomes a lien on your account.

Vacant or neglected houses in Vinita, Welch, Ketchum, Bluejacket and Big Cabin are the usual cases. Title companies notice an unpaid mowing bill right away, so get a complete account printout from the Treasurer before you list or accept an offer.

The Treasurer also manages property the county acquires at its yearly delinquent tax sales, and may sell it with the Board of County Commissioners' approval. A house far behind on taxes can end up there, so do not wait.

sections.h2: Taxes and paperwork when a house sells
sections.html:
At the closing, the escrow or title company calls the Treasurer for the amount owed and pays any balance from what you receive.

A cash purchase moves fast, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. Some steps stay no matter who buys:

  • Request a payoff or tax certificate.
  • Clear any special assessment liens.
  • Sign a deed in the form the clerk requires.
  • Pay documentary stamp tax when recording.

Deeds are recorded with the County Clerk, 210 West Delaware Avenue, Suite 103, Vinita, phone 918-256-2507, open 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM. The index on okcountyrecords.com reaches back to October 1956. Documentary stamp tax under 68 O.S. 3201 is 75 cents per $500 of consideration, on prices above $100.

Sellers in Vinita or out toward Grand Lake can follow one sequence and avoid backtracking. First, call 918-256-2286 and ask the Treasurer for your balance in writing. Second, look at the account for anything beyond the base tax, such as a town's mowing charge. Third, if your valuation looks wrong and the 30 days have not run, file Form 974 before you list, since a lower value helps the next owner too. Fourth, ask the County Clerk at 918-256-2507 how your deed should be formatted. Finally, hand the title company the Treasurer's total and the Clerk's requirements so the closing date holds.

If you own near Grand Lake O' the Cherokees and live elsewhere, mail may go to an address nobody checks. Confirm with the Treasurer that statements reach you, because an unread bill carries the same penalty as a read one. Having the account printout in hand when you list a Vinita house, whether on Historic U.S. 66 or closer to Interstate 44, answers a buyer's first tax question before it is asked.

Out in Welch, Ketchum or along U.S. 69 near Big Cabin, the parcel is often acreage. Know its size and legal description before you list, and copy both from your last recorded deed so the listing, the tax account and the new deed all agree.

A plain sale rarely needs a lawyer, though probate or a split among heirs may. A short call to the offices above usually settles which papers you need.

sections.h2: What Craig County sellers usually run into
sections.html:
Three things cause most of the trouble here: age, distance and paperwork.

  • Inherited houses whose heirs live in several states.
  • Rural lots whose legal descriptions involve acreage and mineral questions.
  • Lake-area properties tied to Grand Lake, which the Pensacola Dam created.
  • Houses with unpaid city charges or back taxes on the account.

Whatever your situation, begin with the Treasurer's balance and the Clerk's records. That way the last week before closing stays calm.

With several heirs, decide early who signs the deed and who covers the tax balance. Collect the death certificate, the probate papers and the latest tax statement, so the title company can confirm the right people may sell. Ask the Clerk what a recordable deed looks like here, since one that misses the format comes back and can delay closing. A cash buyer may take the house as is, yet the taxes and city liens still come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who handles property tax bills in Craig County, Oklahoma?
faqs.a: For a bill or a payment, phone the Treasurer at 918-256-2286 or stop by Suite 104 at 210 W. Delaware in Vinita on a weekday. Questions about what your house is valued at go to the Assessor in the courthouse.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest a Craig County valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days, counted from the mailing date of the valuation notice, and the protest goes to the Assessor in writing. A value that did not change from last year can be protested until the first Monday in April.

faqs.q: When do Craig County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They go delinquent on January 1 if half has not been paid by then. The second half has until April 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Craig County house with taxes still owed?
faqs.a: Yes, and the balance is normally paid out of your proceeds at closing. Start with a written total from the Treasurer, and resolve any special assessments the city sent to the county.

faqs.q: What stamp tax applies to a Craig County deed?
faqs.a: The rate is 75 cents per $500 of consideration under 68 O.S. 3201, owed on prices above $100 when the deed is recorded.
